A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAWN research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and reused material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CALVIN and MetaWorld experiments, real-world xArm trials, bimanual action-prediction results, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports inference timings and qualitative predictions on a newly collected bimanual dataset.

M1.justification: The main architecture, motion representation, losses, and inference equations are unchanged. However, v1 defines a VPP-based DAWN* variant with RGB-plus-motion conditioning, VPP's action expert, and one denoising step. v2 removes that description while retaining its scores under DAWN, leaving uncertain whether the real-world procedure changed or only its labeling and documentation.

E1.justification: v2 adds a locally collected Galaxea R1 Lite dataset with 150 demonstrations and eight plush-toy/pot tasks, illustrated through qualitative motion predictions (Supplement Section 2.3.2, Table 7, Figure 10). This extends existing bimanual coverage with a new tabletop scenario; the original simulation, xArm, DROID, and Galaxea Open-World coverage remains.

E2.justification: MoDE is added to both CALVIN comparisons, with average lengths of 3.39 without external robotic data and 4.01 with external data (Tables 1–2). The other external comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds average inference time per action chunk, measured in milliseconds, to the real-world evaluation. Existing CALVIN evaluation sequences and step limits, xArm trial counts, and the 300-episode bimanual MSE evaluation remain unchanged. CALVIN evaluation details move to the supplement.

E4.justification: The CALVIN representation, pretraining, gripper-view, and diffusion-step ablations are unchanged (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6). v2 adds an efficiency analysis and qualitative cases involving basket placement and coordinated plush-toy/pot manipulation. The existing CALVIN and Galaxea examples are retained or redisplayed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests. The new runtime averages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds MoDE results, qualitative cases, and runtimes of 112.77, 571.89, 190.55, and 319.82 ms for Enhanced DP, pi0, VPP, and DAWN. Table 4 removes the original DAWN row, including apple results of 12 successful lifts and 10 placements, while retaining DAWN*'s 19/19 under DAWN. This does not establish a same-setting improvement. Other quantitative results remain unchanged apart from rounding.

T1.justification: The pixel-motion definitions, three-channel encoding, and denoising equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes substantive theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same core claims: an interpretable two-stage diffusion framework, competitive or state-of-the-art performance, and data-efficient real-world transfer.

C2.justification: v2 adds an argument that direct motion prediction simplifies learning relative to RGB-video prediction and interprets inference overhead as a worthwhile accuracy–speed tradeoff. It removes v1's explanation that the strongest real-world results use a VPP-based variant for matched comparison. Most benchmark interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes Appendix C's complete DAWN* recipe, including VPP initialization, RGB-plus-motion conditioning, the shared action expert, and one-step denoising, despite retaining its results. It also omits CALVIN's specified 10-action replanning interval. Conversely, it adds bimanual data-collection and task details, changes the project-page address, and mentions a supplementary video index. General training hardware and hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: The research positioning is substantially recast around sparse trajectories, future-RGB prediction, and VLAs. The detailed LangToMo comparison is removed, while SuSIE and HAMSTER discussions and a MoDE citation are added. Earlier discussions and citations, including DVD, 3D-VLA, and Octo, disappear. These changes extend beyond citation formatting.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, experimental descriptions are compressed, and CALVIN evaluation details move into the supplement. The appendix is reorganized around dataset descriptions and qualitative results, replacing the DAWN Variants section. Much of the method and conclusion remains textually stable.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure and table relocation and resizing. v2 adds a framework-comparison diagram, a task-definition table, and qualitative displays, and adds a runtime column to Table 4. The original Galaxea figure is shortened in the main text and reproduced fully in the supplement.

improvement.justification: The MoDE comparisons, runtime measurements, and new bimanual examples provide useful additions. However, v2 Table 4 presents v1's DAWN* scores as DAWN while removing the original DAWN results and the appendix explaining the variant's substantially different implementation. This reduces the traceability and reproducibility of an important real-world claim. That loss outweighs the limited additional evidence.
